executiveSummary: GM1930's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 88,341 residents, 89 neighbourhoods, seven BAG places, eleven settlement labels, and two N218 logical links are internally coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only one resident (-0.001%) and is reconciled without rewriting source observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Nissewaard combines dense Spijkenisse, rural Voorne-Putten polders, the Oude Maas, Spui, Hartelkanaal and Bernisse, primary-defence trajectory 20-3, the nationally significant Berenplaat drinking-water production site, and narrow road/metro/seasonal-ferry connections to Rotterdam, Voorne and Hoeksche Waard. The simulator produces exact 2.685367 river and 1.595925 coastal inundation stress, 52,872 river-affected resident-equivalents and service/recovery curves without selecting sea/rivermouth boundary, storm-surge barrier state, defence failure, breach, compartment, arrival, evacuation or dewatering. Coastal, pluvial, heat and wildfire share exactly the same leading neighbourhood order; a controlled fire at the official Hartelpark-West neighbourhood centre ranks its source only 54th of 89. The graph collapses mobility to two series N218 links and omits the Spijkenisserbrug, Hartelbrug, metro, internal roads and ferries; current provincial N218 works/closures in Geervliet-Heenvliet-Zwartewaal are absent from the assigned NDW snapshot. No acute-care department lies inside GM1930, while the nearest straight-line record has limited hours. The model also omits port/Seveso hazardous-material plume/water-contamination cases and the current WSHD salinity/fresh-water intervention at Heenvliet. Public registers and observations remain context, not live topology, capacity, outage, route, care or restoration. Unknown and NoData must never render as zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1930 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1930 as Nissewaard in Zuid-Holland and reports 88,341 residents, density 1,205/km2, 21.8% aged 65 or older and 13,993 one-person households. The generated centre [4.265514344845646, 51.83186822170059] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Eighty-nine neighbourhood rows in 23 districts sum to 88,340 residents, one below the municipality total (-0.001%); households sum to 40,095 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 19,295. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 88,341 without altering source observations.

BAG supplies seven contained woonplaatsen: Abbenbroek, Geervliet, Heenvliet, Hekelingen, Simonshaven, Spijkenisse and Zuidland. BRT supplies eleven labels: seven woonkernen, two deelkernen and two gehuchten, including Berenplaat and Biert.

All 89 rows carry population, age, household, land and water fields, but average household size covers 85/89, home value 74/89, tenure 76/89, cars per household 72/89, benefit fields 79/89, GP/supermarket distance 83/89 and district heat/public charging 0/89. Null, suppression, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Climate Adaptation Strategy Voorne-Putten and municipal climate programme
evidenceSources.edition: Strategy dated 17 March 2021; municipality page and 2024 accountability inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Nissewaard, Voorne aan Zee, WSHD and Zuid-Holland jointly address extreme rain, heat, drought and flooding. The April 2020 stress test and climate dialogues are planning/calibration evidence, not an incident observation or forecast.

The strategy distinguishes dense paved areas, high groundwater, buildings/infrastructure, health and local variability. It says Spijkenisse can face water depths exceeding 20 cm after extreme rain and identifies heat vulnerability and land subsidence; exact source cells/scenarios are not integrated in the simulator.

Municipal accountability states there was not yet a quantified view of progress toward climate-resilient/water-robust outcomes in 2024. Policy targets and completed activities must not be converted to present resilience percentages or guaranteed works.

No governed machine-layer licence, version/refresh, CRS/resolution, coverage and NoData contract was found for the reviewed local stress-test products. Those fields are required before operational map binding.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Voorne-Putten defences, water-control and 2026 fresh-water/salinity intervention
evidenceSources.edition: Current project and crisis pages plus 16 August 2026 salinity notice inspected 3 September 2026
supports: WSHD identifies primary-defence trajectory 20-3 along Hartelkanaal, Oude Maas near Spijkenisse and Spui toward Zuidland. Current reinforcement work addresses potential underwater slope instability and is expected to continue into early 2027; planned work is neither current failure nor proof of event-time reliability.

WSHD explains that lower-river water levels combine North Sea storm surge and Rhine/Meuse discharge, and that primary/regional failures and extreme rain require distinct crisis mechanisms. A selected boundary and failure case is required for local depth.

On 16 August 2026 WSHD reported serious salinization, a Voornse Sluis lock ban, and temporary pumps at Heenvliet routing Kanaal door Voorne water toward Brielse Meer. Bernisse normally feeds Brielse Meer from Spui; the buffer supports Voorne-Putten, Delfland, port industry and Evides.

The temporary measure and HWH register establish control dependencies and valid-time action context, not present chloride at every cell, pump output, road state, reserve, success duration or T+72 restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regional Risk Profile 2022–2025 and Care Risk Profile 2024
evidenceSources.edition: Regional Risk Profile 2022–2025; Care Risk Profile 2024 pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: VRR treats the Rijnmond lower-river area as influenced by both sea storm-surge levels and river discharges, with uncertain high-water timing and possible breach location. It separately lists inner-dike, outer-dike and extreme-rain flooding.

The risk profile covers major port/industrial and hazardous-material incidents, transport, extreme weather, nature fire, cyber and vital-services disruption. Strategic categories do not select a current source, plume, footprint or response action.

The Care Risk Profile states that a water-rich region and complex infrastructure affect care accessibility and that care is fragmented across many partners. GHOR coordination does not itself prove a hospital, ambulance, route, staff, bed or generator is available.

Plans and profiles define roles and preparedness evidence, not event-time command decisions, evacuation/shelter advice, crossings, facility acceptance or restoration. No blanket machine reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Berenplaat drinking-water production and regional dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Operator page published 17 March 2022; 2025 source-water description inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Evides identifies Berenplaat in Spijkenisse as the Netherlands' largest drinking-water production location, serving Rijnmond, Voorne-Putten, Hoeksche Waard, Albrandswaard and Westland and able to back up Kralingen and Baanhoek.

The Berenplaat control room also controls Ouddorp and Haamstede. This is a broad regional dependency, not proof of centralized physical topology, present operational state or a single point of failure.

Evides states Rhine/Meuse surface water is stored and pretreated in Biesbosch reservoirs before transport to Berenplaat and other plants. WSHD's Brielse Meer salinity measures and Berenplaat drinking-water source chains must not be conflated.

Public operator pages reveal role and high-level redundancy only; sensitive topology, current output/load, storage, isolation, power/generator endurance, quality alerts, repair crews and recovery remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Zuid-Holland / Port of Rotterdam / RET-OVapi / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — N218/crossing/metro/ferry and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS snapshot 31 August 2026; current provincial road page and RIVM questionnaire v1.1 inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has only two GM1930 edges, both series sections of physical corridor N218: east toward Rotterdam/A15 and west toward Voorne aan Zee. Their scenario-unit capacity 150 is not measured vehicles/hour and must not be summed as parallel routes.

Port of Rotterdam describes Hartelbrug and Spijkenisserbrug as Spijkenisse's two direct road crossings, with metro beneath Oude Maas. GTFS contains 121 stop areas including Spijkenisse Centrum, Akkers and Heemraadlaan but ProRail has no passenger station. Static identity/schedules do not establish operation, capacity, passengers or restoration.

The province reports N218 works with closures/omleidingen around Geervliet, Heenvliet and Zwartewaal within 31 August–16 October 2026. Exact segments and times require valid-time matching; the deployed NDW snapshot assigns no situation to GM1930, which is not evidence that the corridor is fully open.

No RIVM acute department is inside GM1930. Nearest straight-line references are Franciscus Vlietland 12.778 km with limited hours, Van Weel-Bethesda 14.442 km, Erasmus MC 16.453 km, Ikazia 16.782 km and Franciscus Gasthuis 18.158 km; all except Vlietland report 24/7. Straight-line distance is not ambulance time, crossing/passability or acceptance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / DCMR
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water, grid, communications, education and industrial-risk context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment/public snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; DCMR current public service inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation has 284 GM1930 points: 60 surface-water pumps, 209 weirs, six sluices, seven sewer pumps and two wastewater-treatment points. Capacity exists for 27 surface pumps, but not 33 others, all sewer pumps, weirs, sluices or treatment points; connectivity, units, settings, operation and backup remain unavailable.

One postcode sample maps to Stedin area CM85, Rotterdamse Haven, Voorne aan Zee en omliggende gemeenten, with null existing/required MW, a 5.3 MW withdrawal queue, nine requests and eight planning projects from 2027. It is planning context, not municipality coverage, topology, live load, outage or reserve.

RDI contains 117 antenna installations, including 48 mobile and thirteen fixed-link records; DUO contains 60 education records. Register presence does not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupants, accessibility, supplies or live operation.

DCMR's public industrial oversight describes port-region Seveso fire/explosion, toxic smoke, water pollution and gas-cloud mechanisms that may affect drinking water and ecology. It does not establish a GM1930 incident, plume, current inventory or response and cannot justify invented sensitive topology.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo / KNMI / Nationaal Dataportaal Wegverkeer
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Timestamped Oude Maas/Spui observations and bounded forecast/weather/road coverage
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts 3 September 2026 04:29Z; KNMI/NDW snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Two fresh Waterinfo points are assigned inside GM1930 at 2 September 17:30Z: Spijkenisse Oude Maas 127 cm NAP and Zuidland Spui 57 cm NAP, both publisher-classed normal. They are point observations, not a defence state, municipal water surface, breach or inundation depth.

No Waterinfo forecast is assigned inside GM1930 and the national rolling endpoint returns no T+72 records. Missing forecast coverage is NoData, never stable water, no flood or safety; observations do not drive the canonical river/coastal cases.

No KNMI station and no NDW current situation is assigned inside GM1930 in the reviewed snapshots. This is bounded point/feed and polygon-assignment coverage, not proof of normal weather or open roads, particularly alongside the separate provincial N218 notice.

Waterinfo/NDW are CC0 unless component exceptions apply and KNMI observations are CC BY 4.0. Every observation/forecast/restriction requires publication/issue/observation/valid/retrieval time, spatial support, coverage, uncertainty, affectsSimulation=false and NoData until governed binding.
